info.title: ITMS API
info.description: Unified IT Management System. Every route is versioned in its path (ARCHITECTURE.md §6), every error is an RFC 7807 problem document, and authentication is the session cookie.

get.summary: Issues an antiforgery token for the credential endpoints.

post.summary: Signs in and issues the session cookie.

401.description: Unauthorized

post.summary: Revokes the current session and clears the cookie.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

get.summary: Returns the signed-in account, its roles, and its directory placement.

401.description: Unauthorized

post.summary: Changes the caller's own password and revokes their other sessions.

401.description: Unauthorized

get.summary: Finds active users by name or email, for a picker.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.
No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

get.summary: Lists departments, filtered by search text and optionally including retired ones.

401.description: Unauthorized
No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.
No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

put.summary: Replaces a department's name, code, and description.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

post.summary: Retires a department. Existing references keep resolving.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

post.summary: Brings a retired department back into use.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

get.summary: Lists locations in path order, optionally within one parent or one subtree.

401.description: Unauthorized

post.summary: Creates a location under a parent, or a root organisation.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

get.summary: Reads one location, including its full path.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

put.summary: Renames a location and rewrites the paths of everything beneath it.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

delete.summary: Deletes a location that has no children. A location with children is refused with 409.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

post.summary: Reparents a location, carrying its subtree with it.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

get.summary: Lists ticket categories in picker order, optionally including retired ones.

401.description: Unauthorized
No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.
No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

put.summary: Replaces a ticket category's name, description, and order. Existing tickets follow the rename.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

post.summary: Retires a ticket category. Existing tickets keep resolving it.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

post.summary: Brings a retired ticket category back into use.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

get.summary: Lists ticket priorities most urgent first, optionally including retired ones.

401.description: Unauthorized

post.summary: Creates a ticket priority. The code is chosen here and never changes.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.
No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

put.summary: Replaces a ticket priority's name, description, order, and SLA targets. The code is immutable.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

post.summary: Retires a ticket priority. Existing tickets keep resolving it.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

post.summary: Brings a retired ticket priority back into use.

401.description: No session cookie, or the session it named has expired or been revoked.

get.summary: Counts the queue: the KPI figures and the saved-view totals.
get.description: Scope-wide and deliberately unaffected by any filter — a counter that moved with the filters would describe the filter rather than the queue. A User's counts cover only the tickets they raised. Send dueBefore as the end of your own day; the server falls back to the end of its UTC day.

401.description: Unauthorized

get.summary: Reads the ticket queue, filtered, sorted, and paged.
get.description: A Technician or an Admin reads every ticket; anybody else reads only the tickets they raised. Defaults to newest first.

401.description: Unauthorized

post.description: A User may only raise a ticket for themselves and is refused with 403 for naming anybody else. The requester defaults to the caller and the department to the requester's own.

401.description: Unauthorized

get.summary: Reads one ticket in full, with the head of its timeline.
get.description: Carries an ETag naming the ticket's current version. Send it back as If-Match on a status change to be told the ticket has moved before the change is attempted.

401.description: Unauthorized

get.summary: Reads a ticket's history, newest first.

401.description: Unauthorized

post.summary: Moves a ticket to another status, refusing any transition SPEC.md §2 does not allow.
post.description: Send the ticket's ETag as If-Match to be refused with 412 if it has moved since you read it. Without the header the request proceeds and a lost race is a 409.

401.description: Unauthorized

post.summary: Assigns, reassigns, or unassigns a ticket.
post.description: Send an assigneeId to put a technician in charge, or null to unassign. The first assignment moves the ticket from New to Assigned and unassigning moves it back; reassignment leaves the status alone. Send the ticket's ETag as If-Match to be refused with 412 if it has moved since you read it.

401.description: Unauthorized

get.summary: Reads a ticket's comments, newest first.
get.description: A Technician or an Admin sees internal notes alongside public comments; the requester sees only the public ones, and the total counts only what they can see.

401.description: Unauthorized

post.summary: Posts a comment, or an internal note, on a ticket.
post.description: Set isInternal to keep the comment inside the queue. Only a Technician or an Admin may do that; a requester attempting it is refused with 403 rather than having their note quietly published. Any status accepts a comment, including a closed ticket.

401.description: Unauthorized

get.summary: Reads a ticket's attachments, newest first.
get.description: Metadata only. Internal attachments are absent for anybody but a Technician or an Admin, and the total counts only what the caller can see.

401.description: Unauthorized

post.summary: Attaches a file to a ticket.
post.description: Multipart form with a 'file' part and an optional 'isInternal' field. The extension must be on the allowlist and the file's leading bytes must agree with it; the declared media type is ignored. Only a Technician or an Admin may attach an internal file.

401.description: Unauthorized

get.description: Re-checks the ticket and the audience on every request: an attachment on a ticket the caller cannot read, or an internal one they are not staff for, is 404 either way. Always served as a download, never inline.

401.description: Unauthorized

isInternal.description:
True to write a note only the queue can read. A User sending this is refused with 403
rather than quietly downgraded — see `HelpdeskErrors.InternalCommentForbidden`.

assigneeId.description:
The technician taking the ticket on, or `null` to unassign it. A null
is a deliberate instruction, not an omitted field: unassigning returns the ticket to
`New`, and is refused once work has started.

displayName.description: The name shown throughout the product.

roles.description: Their roles. The client uses these to hide what a role cannot use; hiding is never the enforcement (ARCHITECTURE.md §7).

AuthenticatedUserResponse.description:
The account the caller is signed in as. Returned by both `/login` and
`/me`, so the client has one shape to hold for "who am I" however it got there.

currentPassword.description: The password in force. Proving possession is what stops a borrowed session changing it.

newPassword.description: The replacement. Checked against the password policy server-side.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: A password change by the account holder.

status.description:
The status to move to. `Assigned` is not accepted here: a ticket becomes assigned
by assigning it to somebody (WP-1.6), so that the status and the assignee arrive
together. `New` is not accepted either — nothing returns to it.

resolutionNotes.description:
What was done. Required and non-blank when Status is
`Resolved`, and rejected for every other destination, because no other transition
records a resolution and silently dropping the text would lose it.

code.description: A short code such as `FIN`, or `null`. Unique when present.

name.description: The node's own name. Unique among its siblings, case-insensitively.

kind.description: Which level of the hierarchy it is.

parentId.description: The parent node, or `null` to create a root organisation.

description.description: What belongs in this category, or `null`.

sortOrder.description: Where it sits in a picker. Ties are broken by name.

code.description: The stable machine identifier, lower-cased on the way in. Unique and immutable.

name.description: The display name. Unique, case-insensitively, and editable.

description.description: What this priority is for, or `null`.

rank.description: Urgency order, lowest first. Ties are broken by name.

responseTargetMinutes.description: Minutes from creation within which a technician should respond.

resolutionTargetMinutes.description: Minutes from creation within which the ticket should be resolved.

subject.description: The one-line summary. SPEC.md §2 calls this the title, and a form should label it so.

description.description: What is wrong, in the requester's words.

categoryId.description: What the ticket is about. Must name a category that has not been retired.

priorityId.description: How urgent it is. Must name a priority that has not been retired.

requesterId.description:
Who the ticket is for, or `null` for the caller. Only a Technician or
an Admin may name somebody else.

departmentId.description:
The department to file it against, or `null` to take the requester's
own.

token.description: The request token, sent back in HeaderName.

headerName.description: The header the token belongs in, so the client never hard-codes it.

CsrfTokenResponse.description: The token the browser needs before it may post to a credential endpoint.

DepartmentResponse.description: A department as the API renders it.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated in the body as RFC 7807 allows.

code.description: The machine-readable error identifier, e.g. auth.antiforgery_failed. Present on every problem this system produces itself; absent on one produced by the framework.

LocationKind.description:
What a node in the location tree represents. The five levels SPEC.md §5 names:
Organization → Site → Building → Floor/Area → Room.

name.description: Its own name — "Room G-04", not the whole path.

kind.description: Which level of the hierarchy it is.

parentId.description: Its parent, or `null` at the root.

path.description: The full display path from the root, which is what other modules also receive.

depth.description: How far below the root it sits.

childCount.description:
How many nodes sit directly beneath it. Carried so a caller can render the tree and
know whether a delete will be refused before it tries.

LocationResponse.description: A location as the API renders it.

userName.description: The sign-in name or the email address; either is accepted.

password.description: The password. Never logged, never echoed, never stored outside its hash.

parentId.description:
The new parent, or `null` to move the node to the root — which only
an Organization may be.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated in the body as RFC 7807 allows.

code.description: The machine-readable error identifier, e.g. auth.antiforgery_failed. Present on every problem this system produces itself; absent on one produced by the framework.

errors.description: Per-field validation messages, keyed by camel-cased field name. Present only on a validation failure.

SlaState.description:
Where one of a ticket's two SLA clocks stands: SPEC.md §2's "approaching (80%
consumed) and breached", plus the three states those two flags only make sense
against.

number.description: Its human-readable number, so a toast can name it.

previousAssigneeId.description: Who held it before, or `null` if nobody did.

previousAssigneeName.description: Their display name as the ticket had cached it, or `null`.

assigneeId.description: Who holds it now, or `null` after an unassignment.

assigneeName.description: Their display name, cached on the row at this moment.

changedAt.description: When the assignment happened, in UTC.

allowedNextStatuses.description:
Where the ticket may go next, straight from the state machine, for the same reason
TicketStatusChangeResponse carries it: WP-1.10 must not render a
transition the server would refuse.

TicketAssignmentResponse.description: What a ticket looks like immediately after its assignee changed.

id.description: The attachment's id. What the download route names.

fileName.description: The name the uploader's file had.

contentType.description: The media type the download will declare.

isInternal.description: True when the requester cannot see it. Always false in a payload they receive.

uploadedByName.description: Their display name at the time.

TicketAttachmentResponse.description: A file attached to a ticket, as the API describes it.

id.description: The category's id. What a ticket stores, and what a rename does not change.

sortOrder.description: Where it sits in a picker.

TicketCategoryResponse.description: A ticket category as the API renders it.

TicketChangeKind.description: Which dimension of a ticket a history entry records having moved.

isInternal.description: True when this line is invisible to the requester.

authorName.description: Their display name at the time.

TicketCommentResponse.description: One line of a ticket's conversation, as the API renders it.

all.description: Every ticket the caller can see, in any status.

open.description: Tickets still being worked: New, Assigned, In Progress, or Waiting.

overdue.description: Tickets whose resolution clock has breached.

dueToday.description: Open tickets due before the instant the caller named as the end of their day.

mine.description:
The caller's own workload — tickets assigned to them if they work the queue, or
tickets they raised if they do not. The same rule WP-1.9's "My tickets" view follows,
so the chip and its count mean one thing.

TicketCountersResponse.description: The queue's headline numbers: what the KPI row shows and what the saved views count.

status.description: Where it sits in the workflow.

categoryName.description: That category's name, as it reads now.

priorityName.description: That priority's name, as it reads now.

priorityCode.description: That priority's stable key, for colour and for rules.

requesterName.description: Their display name, cached at creation.

departmentId.description: The department it is filed against.

departmentName.description: That department's name, cached at creation.

resolutionNotes.description: What was done, once it has been resolved. Kept through a reopen.

relatedAssetId.description: The asset it concerns, or `null`. WP-2.5 sets it.

relatedAlertId.description: The alert it was raised from, or `null`. WP-3.7 sets it.

dueAt.description:
When resolution is due, pauses included. The same instant as `sla.resolutionDueAt`,
kept at the top level because the queue sorts on it and the wire has carried it since
WP-1.5.

sla.description: Both SLA clocks, and where each stands right now.

allowedNextStatuses.description:
The statuses this ticket may legally move to next, straight from the state
machine. Empty once the ticket is terminal.

history.description:
The head of the ticket's timeline, newest first — at most
int TicketDetailResponse.EmbeddedHistoryCount entries.

hasMoreHistory.description:
True when the ticket's timeline is longer than what
IReadOnlyList<TicketHistoryEntryResponse> TicketDetailResponse.History carries, so a client knows to offer the paged endpoint.

comments.description:
The head of the ticket's conversation, newest first — at most
int TicketDetailResponse.EmbeddedThreadCount comments the caller is allowed to read.

hasMoreComments.description:
True when there are more comments the caller may read than
IReadOnlyList<TicketCommentResponse> TicketDetailResponse.Comments carries.

attachments.description:
The ticket's attachments, newest first — at most int TicketDetailResponse.EmbeddedThreadCount
of the ones the caller is allowed to see. Metadata only; the bytes come from the
download route.

hasMoreAttachments.description:
True when there are more attachments the caller may see than
IReadOnlyList<TicketAttachmentResponse> TicketDetailResponse.Attachments carries.

TicketDetailResponse.description: One ticket in full, as the detail screen reads it.

fromValue.description: What it read before, or `null` when there was nothing there.

toValue.description: What it reads now, or `null` when the change cleared it.

sequence.description:
Where this line sits among the lines the same change wrote. Entries sharing an
OccurredAt came from one change and are meant to be read together.

actorId.description: Who made it, or `null` when the system did.

actorName.description: Their display name at the time, or `null`.

TicketHistoryEntryResponse.description: One line of a ticket's timeline, as the API renders it.

subject.description: The one-line summary. SPEC.md §2 calls this the title, and a UI should label it so.

status.description: Where it sits in the workflow.

categoryName.description: That category's name, as it reads now.

priorityName.description: That priority's name, as it reads now.

priorityCode.description: That priority's stable key, for colour and for rules.

priorityRank.description: Its ordering weight, so a client can sort a page it already holds.

requesterName.description: Their display name, cached at creation.

departmentId.description: The department it is filed against.

departmentName.description: That department's name, cached at creation.

assigneeId.description: The technician responsible, or `null` while unassigned.

createdAt.description: When it was raised (UTC). The queue's "age" column is computed from this.

dueAt.description:
When resolution is due, pauses included. The same instant as `sla.resolutionDueAt`,
kept at the top level because the queue sorts on it.

sla.description: Both SLA clocks, and where each stands right now.

TicketListItemResponse.description: One row of the ticket queue, as the API renders it.

id.description: The priority's id. What a ticket stores.

code.description: The stable machine identifier — `critical`, `high`. Fixed for the life of the row.

responseTargetMinutes.description: Minutes from creation within which a technician should respond.

resolutionTargetMinutes.description: Minutes from creation within which the ticket should be resolved.

TicketPriorityResponse.description: A ticket priority as the API renders it.

responseTargetMinutes.description: Minutes the priority allowed for a response when the ticket was filed.

responseDueAt.description: When the response target expires. A pause never moves it.

responseWarnAt.description: When 80% of the response target is consumed.

respondedAt.description:
When somebody first answered — the first public comment from anybody but the requester,
or the resolution — or `null` while nobody has.

resolutionTargetMinutes.description: Minutes the priority allowed for a resolution when the ticket was filed.

resolutionDueAt.description:
When the resolution target expires, every pause so far included. The same instant the
ticket's own `dueAt` carries; it is repeated here so the SLA object reads on its
own.

resolutionWarnAt.description: When 80% of the resolution target is consumed.

resolvedAt.description:
When the resolution clock stopped, or `null` while it runs. The ticket's
own resolution instant, seen from the SLA's side.

pausedAt.description: When the ticket entered Waiting, or `null` when the clock is running.

responseState.description: Where the response clock stands. Filled by TicketSlaResponse TicketSlaResponse.Assessed(TicketStatus status, DateTimeOffset now).

resolutionState.description: Where the resolution clock stands. Filled by TicketSlaResponse TicketSlaResponse.Assessed(TicketStatus status, DateTimeOffset now).

isPaused.description: Whether the resolution clock is parked because the ticket is Waiting.

pausedSeconds.description: How long the ticket has spent Waiting in total, in whole seconds.

TicketSlaResponse.description:
A ticket's two SLA clocks as the API renders them: what was promised, when each
deadline falls, and where each clock stands right now.

TicketStatus.description: Where a ticket sits in the workflow SPEC.md §2 defines.

number.description: Its human-readable number, so a toast can name it.

status.description: The status it is in now.

changedAt.description: When the move happened, in UTC.

resolvedAt.description: When it was resolved, or `null` — cleared by a reopen.

allowedNextStatuses.description:
Where it may go next, straight from the state machine. WP-1.10 must not render a
transition button the server would refuse, and reading it from here is what stops the
table being written a second time in TypeScript. Empty from a terminal state.

TicketStatusChangeResponse.description: What a ticket looks like immediately after a status change.

code.description: The short code, or `null` to clear it.

description.description: Free text, or `null` to clear it.
Free text, or `null` to clear it.

name.description: The display name. Every ticket already filed under this category follows the rename.

description.description: What belongs in it, or `null` to clear it.

sortOrder.description: Where it sits in a picker.

description.description: What this priority is for, or `null` to clear it.

responseTargetMinutes.description: Minutes from creation within which a technician should respond.

resolutionTargetMinutes.description: Minutes from creation within which the ticket should be resolved.

displayName.description: The name to show on a ticket, comment, or asset history row.

isActive.description: False once deactivated. A deactivated user still owns their history (invariant 9).

roles.description:
The roles the account holds, from the three `ItmsRoles` names. Carried because
eligibility rules are a module's own business but the role that decides them is
Identity's: Helpdesk may only assign a ticket to a technician (WP-1.6), and without
this it would have to either reference `Modules.Identity` or trust the caller.
A membership list rather than a workflow flag, so no one module's question is baked
into the contract.

UserSummary.description:
The fields another module is allowed to know about a user. It carries no
credential state of any kind — that never leaves Identity.

sessionCookie.description: HttpOnly session cookie, issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login and revoked server-side by POST /api/v1/auth/logout. The browser sends it automatically; it cannot be read by script and is never held in browser storage.
sessionCookie.name: itms.session
